writeup.headline: Zoom rates Hold at 64, one point below Buy, as strong cash generation offsets slow growth.
writeup.thesis: Zoom scores 64, a Hold that sits just 1 point below the Buy line. The business is highly profitable and cash-rich: a 77.3% gross margin, 23.7% operating margin and 38.6% free cash flow margin, a diluted share count down 2.8% year on year, and net cash with no debt give it top marks on quality and balance sheet. Growth is the weak spot, with TTM revenue growth of 5.0%, latest-quarter growth of 4.9%, and growth slowed by 0.5 pp from the previous quarter. Valuation is moderate in absolute terms at 6.0x sales, 15.6x free cash flow and 19.2x EV/EBIT, with FCF yield 1.4 pp above the 10-year Treasury yield, and overall sits near the middle of its own history, though P/S is more expensive than at 48 of the last 61 month-ends. Recent news leans mildly positive after Zoomtopia's long-term targets and an Oppenheimer upgrade, while the shares trail SPY and QQQ over the last 126 trading days.
key_risks: Revenue growth is only around 5% and slowed by 0.5 pp, leaving little room for disappointment
Stock-based compensation equals 14.6% of revenue, a real cost behind the strong free cash flow
Shares are 4.4 pp behind SPY and 5.2 pp behind QQQ over the last 126 trading days
Long-term targets of 6–8% growth and about 40% operating margin must be delivered to justify current sentiment
AI-driven competition in communications software could pressure pricing or the enterprise mix
what_would_change: A 1-point score gain would move the rating to Buy, for example from growth re-accelerating above the latest 4.9% pace or firmer price trend
Better relative performance against SPY and QQQ would lift the trend score from 57
A drop to Sell would need about 20 points of deterioration, such as revenue turning to decline alongside negative news on guidance or analysts
A reversal of the positive guidance and analyst news would cut the news score from 60 and push the rating further from Buy
